_comment: The route table. owner JS = registered by app.js (compared with the real Express router stack by tools/build-overview.js --check). `derived` rows stand for routes generated from site/site.json. `tryIt` rows get a live button.
intro: Express answers every request a browser makes. The JSON API is small: all its bodies are JSON and every error has the same shape, {error:{code,status,message}}.

groups.title: Pages and files
groups.blurb: Defined by site/site.json and the media rules; nothing else on disk is served.

groups.title: Health and the site map
groups.blurb: What the browser may know. Never a secret.

groups.title: The Design Studio
groups.blurb: What the website adds for the studio. The studio's own API (/api/session, /api/rooms, /api/vision, /api/pipeline, /api/ai, /api/admin) is its own: see swatchroom/README.md. With STUDIO_REQUIRE_PASSCODE off (the default) it has no passcode; its costly and private routes (/api/ai, /api/rooms, /api/vision, /api/pipeline, /api/check) need a signed-in, finished account (server/auth/index.js apiGate), and server/lib/studioShield.js gives each account only its own rooms and rate limits those routes. Any other capital letters in /api (/API/rooms) are 404 (server/middleware/canonical.js).

groups.title: Analytics
groups.blurb: Where a page sends its PostHog events. Never a secret: the key is a write-only project key.

groups.title: Sign-in and accounts
groups.blurb: Everything the sign-in page and the account page call (server/routes/auth.js). Same-site JSON only, never cached, every route counted against a per-address ceiling. A one-time code goes to an e-mail address or a mobile number; the answer to asking for one is the same for a member and a stranger. See README, "Sign-in, accounts and the CRM".

groups.title: Sign-in admin API
groups.blurb: What the admin panel (not built yet) will call to manage rate limits and the sign-in settings, read the security log and look after the CRM queue (server/routes/authAdmin.js). Needs Authorization: Bearer <AUTH_ADMIN_TOKEN>; with no token set every route answers 404 as if it did not exist.

groups.title: Inspiration import
groups.blurb: Paste an address, get a picture to crop, send it to the Design Studio (target C3). The address is read by gallery-dl for the sites in site/inspiration/sources.js, directly for a picture link, and by the page's own named picture for any other web page, always through public addresses only (server/lib/inspiration/safeFetch.js). The browser never names a picture address: it gets one-use tokens. All three API routes need a signed-in, finished account (or, with sign-in switched off, are limited by address).

routes.summary: The pages, from site/site.json.
routes.request: No body. The route list comes from site/site.json (`pages.<key>.route`).
routes.response: 200 text/html, Cache-Control: no-cache, conditional requests, plus the headers the page lists in site/site.json (`pages.<key>.headers`). Every page but the landing page (`access: "signed-in"` in site.json) needs a signed-in, finished account: a visitor without one gets 302 to /login?next=<the route>, whatever way the address was written (aliases, capitals, encoded letters); the private pages are `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` with `Vary: Cookie`.

errors.when: Unexpected Host header
The built page is missing (run npm run build:site)
Not signed in (or the sign-up form is not finished): to /login
The account database is down: nothing is let through

routes.summary: Aliases redirect (301) to the canonical route (also /studio and /swatchroom, which lead to the Design Studio); design-time names such as Design Studio.dc.html redirect (302). A name that differs only by capitals or a trailing slash (/Materials, /materials/) redirects (301) to the page.
routes.request: No body. Aliases and `legacy_names` come from site/site.json; names are compared decoded.
routes.response: 301 or 302 with a Location header.

routes.summary: This page.
routes.response: 200 text/html, docs/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.html.

routes.summary: The Coming soon page. Any other address that is a page nobody has built yet gets the same page, with a 404 status (not for files, /api or /media).
routes.response: 200 text/html (404 for an address that is no page), Cache-Control: no-cache.

routes.summary: Photos and videos from media/.
routes.request: No body. Only the extensions listed in site/site.json `media.extensions`; Range requests work.
routes.response: 200 or 206 with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600.

errors.when: Other extension, a dot-segment, or traversal (/media/../.env, /media/%2e%2e/.env)

routes.summary: No icon; answers quietly so the browser stops asking.
routes.response: 204 No Content.

routes.summary: Is the server up, which version, and is the Design Studio running?
routes.response: {ok:true, version, studio:{running, database}, auth:{ready, gate, reasons}}. studio.database is whether the studio's MongoDB is connected; the studio opens without it, so it never makes ok false. auth.reasons are coarse codes (no-secret, no-channel, no-database) saying why sign-in cannot work; the sentences are in the start-up banner and the admin API.

errors.when: Unexpected Host header

routes.summary: The public view of site/site.json: names and routes, no file paths, no headers.
routes.response: {name, pages:[{key, label, nav, description, route}], docs:[...], connections}

routes.summary: Start the Design Studio's cold start: wake its GPU services early. The landing page and the studio page call it as soon as they open.
routes.request: {from?: 'landing' | 'studio'}, only used for the log line. No passcode: it is the website's route, so a visitor who has not signed in to the studio yet wakes it too.
routes.response: {warming: n}: how many services were started, answered at once (the wake-up runs in the background). {warming: 0, reason} when there was nothing to do: everything already warm or starting, STUDIO_WARMUP=off, or no studio mounted.

errors.when: Not application/json
Origin differs from Host
Unexpected Host header

routes.summary: Tells a page where to send its PostHog events. Every page asks once (site/patches/snippets/analytics.js), so no key is written into the pages.
routes.response: {enabled: false} with no key, a malformed key or host, or when the site is opened as localhost. Otherwise {enabled: true, key, host, replay}.

errors.when: Unexpected Host header

routes.summary: What the sign-in page may offer: which ways in are open, the Google client id, how long a code works.
routes.response: {ready, channels:{email,sms,google}, googleClientId, codeLength, resendSeconds, signupOpen, requireFirm, confirm:{email,phone}, smsCountryCodes, routes, crmDeletes}. `confirm` says for which of e-mail / phone the second contact detail is confirmed with a code at sign-up. `routes` are the only places a person may be sent after signing in. Nothing secret.

errors.when: Unexpected Host header
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)

routes.summary: Who is signed in (this browser's cookie).
routes.response: {authenticated:false} or {authenticated:true, user:{name, firm, individual, email, emailVerified, phone, phoneVerified, googleLinked, profileComplete, needs}}. `needs` lists what is missing: name, email, phone, firm, and email-confirm / phone-confirm (typed but not yet confirmed with a code). Never an internal id.

errors.when: Unexpected Host header
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)
Sign-in is not set up or its database is down (reason not-ready / unavailable)

routes.summary: Send a one-time code to an e-mail address or mobile number. The one box on the sign-in page: it works out which it is. The answer is the same whether or not there is an account.
routes.request: {identifier}: an e-mail address or a mobile number (10 digits, or +country).
routes.response: {ok, challengeId, channel:'email'|'sms', to (masked), resendIn, expiresIn, codeLength}. The code is never in the answer.

errors.when: Not application/json
A foreign Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site (reason cross-site)
Unexpected Host header
Not an e-mail or mobile number (reason invalid-identifier); a throw-away address or a country not on the list
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)
Wait between codes (cooldown), too many codes to that address (rate-limited), too many wrong codes (locked)
No sender for that way in, or the site's daily ceiling is reached
The sender failed (send-failed)

routes.summary: Check the code. Right: signs in (and makes the account the first time) by setting the session cookie. A wrong code costs one of five tries.
routes.request: {challengeId, code, next?}. `next` is only used if it is exactly one of the site's routes.
routes.response: {ok, created, needsProfile, redirectTo, user}. redirectTo is always a route of this site. The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax; __Host- and Secure on HTTPS.

errors.when: Not application/json
A foreign Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site (reason cross-site)
Wrong, expired or used code (reasons wrong-code, expired, too-many-attempts, invalid-code), with attemptsLeft
New accounts are closed (signup-closed)
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)
Sign-in is not set up or its database is down (reason not-ready / unavailable)

routes.summary: A one-use value for Google's token, tied to this browser by an HttpOnly cookie (terucon_gn), so a token cannot be replayed or used from another browser.
routes.response: {nonce}: pass it to Google's initialize(). The cookie holds the secret it was made from.

errors.when: Not application/json
A foreign Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site (reason cross-site)
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)
Google sign-in is not set up (AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)

routes.summary: Sign in with a Google ID token (One Tap / the button). The token's signature, issuer, audience, expiry, verified e-mail and nonce are all checked on the server.
routes.response: As /api/auth/verify. A new Google account is made at once from Google's name and verified e-mail; phone and firm are asked for next (needsProfile).

errors.when: Not application/json
A foreign Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site (reason cross-site)
Token not good (reason google-wrong-audience, google-expired, google-email-unverified, google-wrong-nonce ...)
That e-mail is linked to a different Google account (google-conflict)
New accounts are closed
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)
Google sign-in is not set up

routes.summary: Save the sign-up form or the profile page: name, firm (or "individual"), and the e-mail / mobile number that was not yet proved. A confirmed one is not changed by typing.
routes.request: {name?, firm?, individual?, email?, phone?}. Text only; HTML, link-like text and values starting = + - @ are refused.
routes.response: {ok, user}. The sign-up is finished (user.profileComplete) only when nothing is missing, which includes confirming the typed e-mail / number with a code (/api/auth/contact/start and /confirm) where that way of sending is available. A finished sign-up is queued for the CRM.

errors.when: Not signed in (reason auth-required)
Not application/json
A foreign Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site (reason cross-site)
A field is not acceptable (reason invalid-profile, with field)
Too many requests from this address (reason rate-limited)
Sign-in is not set up or its database is down (reason not-ready / unavailable)

routes.curl: curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -b 'terucon_session=...' -d '{"name":"Priya Sharma","phone":"9876543210","firm":"AB Constructions"}' http://localhost:8080/api/auth/profile

routes.summary: A firm name to suggest for a business e-mail address: from the domain, or (setting firm.lookup = website) from the firm's own website, read with SSRF protection. Only for somebody who has already proved an address or number.
routes.request: {email?}: a typed address; otherwise the account's own confirmed address or Google workspace domain.
routes.response: {name, source:'domain'|'website', domain} or all null (a free mailbox, nothing found, switched off).

routes.response: {ok, challengeId, to (masked), ...}

routes.summary: Delete the account: its Design Studio rooms and photos first (if that fails the account stays), what waits in the CRM queue, every session and code, then the account.
routes.response: {ok}. The cookie is cleared.

No confirm, or a wrong code

routes.summary: Every sign-in setting with its value, default, bounds, unit and a label: enough to draw a form.
routes.response: {values, defaults, changed, version, updatedAt, schema:[{key, group, label, help, type, default, min, max, unit, options}]}

A valid admin token is needed (reason unauthorized)

Every value has hard bounds; a bad save changes nothing.
routes.request: {settings: {"limits.otpStartPerIpPerHour": 20, "crm.module": null}}. null puts a setting back to its default.
routes.response: The same as GET, after the save. Effective on the next request.

routes.summary: The sign-in page: one box for an e-mail address or mobile number, the code, the "tell us about you" form (with a firm name suggested from a business e-mail), and Google One Tap. Aliases: /signin, /sign-in, /signup, /sign-up, /register.
routes.request: No body. ?next=/materials names where to go afterwards (only a route of the site is used).
routes.response: 200 text/html with its own Content-Security-Policy built from the page (its one script and style by hash; Google's sign-in script only from the addresses Google documents) and Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

routes.summary: Your details: edit name and firm, confirm or change an e-mail or number, sign out (here or everywhere), delete the account.
routes.response: 200 text/html with a strict Content-Security-Policy. Members only (302 to /login otherwise).

errors.when: Not signed in

routes.summary: The browser modules and stylesheet of the import (site/inspiration/): a fixed list of names, nothing else in the folder.
routes.request: No body. The names are `ASSETS` in server/routes/inspiration.js; a test checks the list against the folder.
routes.response: 200 text/javascript or text/css, Cache-Control: no-cache, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Public: it is code, with no secrets and no data.

errors.when: Any other name, a dot-segment, other capitals

routes.summary: Whether importing from links works on this server, the sites it reads, and the biggest picture it takes.
routes.response: {enabled, ready, sites: [{id, label, kinds}], maxFileMb}. `ready` is false when gallery-dl (python/.venv) is not installed; picture links and web pages still work then.

errors.when: Not signed in
The sign-up form is not finished, or a foreign Origin
Sign-in is not available, or importing is switched off (INSPIRATION_IMPORT=off) or not set up (reason off / not-set-up)

routes.summary: What an address is, and the pictures it holds. A Pinterest pin or board, an Unsplash, Pexels, Flickr, Behance, Imgur or Wikimedia Commons page (read by gallery-dl with that site's own options), a link to a picture file, or any other web page (its own named main picture).
routes.request: {input}: what was pasted or typed; the first usable address in it is used.
routes.response: {type: 'source'|'direct'|'page', kind: 'photo'|'collection', source: {id, label}, shape, title, approximate, items: [{token, preview, width, height, title}]}. Tokens belong to the account, last 15 minutes and stand for an address the server worked out itself; the picture addresses are never sent. Answers are remembered 10 minutes per address.

errors.when: No usable address (reason bad-address)
Not signed in
The sign-up form is not finished, or a foreign Origin
Not found, or nothing usable there (reason not-found / empty)
Instagram, Facebook or X (reason login: the message says to upload), a profile or other page of a known site (unsupported), or something private (private)
30 new addresses an hour per account, 90 per network address; Retry-After says when (reason rate)
The other site did not answer or refused (reason blocked / failed)
Three imports are already running (busy), or off / not set up
The other site took too long (reason timeout)
Not application/json

routes.summary: One of the pictures a resolve gave, checked, from this site's own address so the browser may crop it.
routes.request: No body. The token is from /api/inspiration/resolve, for the same account.
routes.response: 200 with the picture's bytes (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF, decided from the bytes, not from what the other site said), X-Picture-Size, Cache-Control: private, no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. At most 25 MB (INSPIRATION_MAX_FILE_MB) and 64 million pixels; fetched through public addresses only, at most 3 redirects, each checked again.

errors.when: Not signed in
The sign-up form is not finished, or a foreign Origin
Unknown, expired or someone else's token (reason expired)
Too big in bytes or pixels (reason too-big)
Not a picture we take: HTML, SVG, HEIC ... (reason not-an-image)
The site said private / needs a sign-in, or the address is not a public website (reason private / blocked)
90 downloads an hour per account (reason rate)
The site would not give the picture (reason status / network)

routes.summary: The Inspiration page: a box for a link, Paste and Import buttons, upload and drag-and-drop, the sites it reads, and the pictures imported lately in this browser.
routes.response: 200 text/html with a strict Content-Security-Policy built from the page (server/lib/csp.js, `strict+images`): its own script and style only, `blob:` pictures and the picture hosts of the sites it reads. Private: Cache-Control: private, no-cache, Vary: Cookie.
